findings.trigger: set_config() (:66-84) keeps only name, docker_name, allowed_actions and info of every server and drops display_name, active, order, container_name, allow_detailed_status. get_cached_servers() therefore returns two different shapes for the same call: while the cache is valid (set less than 15 min ago) the trimmed list from get_servers() (:281), afterwards the full list from the config service (:283). A consumer that reads server['display_name'] or server.get('active', True) or server.get('order', 999) gets the docker name / 'active' / 999 for the first 15 minutes after start and the real values after that, with no error either way. controllable_entries() in this very section reads exactly display_name, container_name and order; whether it is fed from get_cached_servers() I cannot see.
findings.suggestion: Either keep the full server dicts in the cache (the memory saving of a few dozen dicts is negligible next to the discord.py object graph, as the comments at :120-122 already concede), or make get_servers()/get_cached_servers() document and enforce that only name/docker_name/allowed_actions/info are available - and check every caller for other keys.
findings.unsure_why: The shape difference is certain from the code; whether any caller reads one of the dropped keys from get_cached_servers()/get_servers() depends on code outside this section.

findings.trigger: Cache older than max_cache_age (15 min, :240) and the access count reaches a multiple of 100: get_config() calls _cleanup_if_needed(), which empties _cache and sets _last_update=None (:118-119), and then in the same call returns self._cache.copy() == {} as 'the configuration' (:108). From then on, until somebody calls set_config() again, get_config() returns {} and the typed getters return their defaults silently: get_language() -> 'en', get_timezone() -> 'Europe/Berlin', get_channel_permissions() -> {} (no channel has any permission), get_servers() -> [], get_guild_id() -> None. None of these methods consults is_valid(); only the module-level helpers get_cached_servers()/get_cached_guild_id() do (:280, :292). Between minute 15 and the 100th access the same getters serve stale data and is_valid() already says False.
findings.suggestion: Make the class getters honest about expiry: either have get_config()/get_servers()/get_language()/... raise or return None when the cache is empty or expired (so callers fall back to the config service, as the module-level helpers do), or drop the age-based clearing entirely and let set_config() be the only thing that changes the content. At minimum, get_config() must not return the dict it has just emptied.
findings.unsure_why: The code path is certain. Whether any caller uses ConfigCache.get_config()/get_language()/get_channel_permissions() directly (rather than the module-level helpers that check is_valid()) is outside this section; if none does, the effect is only wasted I/O.

findings.trigger: guild_id stored in the configuration as a JSON number (int) instead of a digit string: the check `isinstance(guild_id_str, str) and guild_id_str.isdigit()` fails and get_guild_id() returns None, i.e. 'not configured', although a guild id is present. The fallback path get_cached_guild_id() (:296-298) repeats the identical check, so the two agree on the wrong answer and nothing is logged. The same check exists twice and can drift.
findings.suggestion: Accept int as well (`isinstance(v, int) or (isinstance(v, str) and v.isdigit())`) in one shared helper used by both places, and log at WARNING when a guild_id is present but not usable.
findings.unsure_why: Whether the config service ever stores guild_id as an int (e.g. after a hand edit of config.json or an old migration) is outside this section.

findings.trigger: Any configuration: _get_cache_size_mb() uses sys.getsizeof(self._cache), which measures only the outer dict object (a few hundred bytes for a dict of ~20 keys), never the nested server list, permissions or strings. get_memory_stats()['cache_size_mb'] and the debug line at :47 therefore report ~0.00 MB regardless of content, presented as the cache size.
findings.suggestion: Either measure recursively (walk the nested structure) or drop the number from the stats; a wrong number is worse than none.

findings.trigger: The groups file cannot be read (OSError) while an admin panel for a group is opened or redrawn after a press: group_is_running() returns False from a bare `except OSError: return False` with no log line - the only one of the four group readers in this file that says nothing - and running_state_for() (:355-357) wraps that into (False, True), i.e. 'not running, status KNOWN'. The panel then confidently draws the start button. In the same situation group_panel_embed() logs an error and shows 'This group does not exist any more.' (:171), which is a wrong statement: the group exists, its file is unreadable. (_maintenance_button at :335-337 swallows the same OSError silently as well.)
findings.suggestion: Log the OSError in group_is_running() like the other three readers, and let it signal 'unknown' (e.g. return Optional[bool] or raise) so running_state_for() can answer (False, False) and the panel is drawn gold as for a container whose status is unknown. Give group_panel_embed() a distinct message for 'could not be read' versus 'does not exist'.

findings.trigger: The groups file is present but not valid JSON (or otherwise malformed) and get_group_service().get_groups() raises a ValueError/JSONDecodeError/KeyError rather than an OSError: the `except OSError` at :70 does not catch it, group_entries() propagates it, and controllable_entries() (:122) - which is 'one list, asked twice' for both admin buttons - fails as a whole. The docstring promises the opposite: 'a failure here costs the groups, not the menu' (:71-73). The same OSError-only pattern is at :165 (group_panel_embed) and :220 (group_config_for).
findings.suggestion: Either widen the catch to what the group service can actually raise on a bad file (ValueError/KeyError/TypeError alongside OSError), or have get_group_service() guarantee that a corrupt file surfaces only as OSError/a documented exception - and pin that with a test, because the promise in the docstring is otherwise unfulfilled.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see services/config/group_service.py. If get_groups() already converts every parse error into OSError or an empty list, the catch is complete and this is not a finding.

findings.trigger: A container's admin panel is built: admin_panel_embed() calls cog._generate_status_embed_and_view() (:274), which already returns the running state as the third value, discards it (_running), and then calls running_state_for() -> cog.get_status(config) a second time (:280, :358) to choose the colour. Two status queries for one panel; if the container changes state between the two awaits (an action was just pressed - that is exactly when the panel is redrawn) the embed body shows one state and the colour another, and the second query is a second round trip to Docker on every redraw.
findings.suggestion: Use the _running value that _generate_status_embed_and_view() already returned for the colour (or pass the status result into it), so the body and the colour come from one observation.

findings.trigger: A private (ephemeral) view whose self.message is a plain discord.Message rather than an InteractionMessage - e.g. set by a caller from interaction.message after response.edit_message(view=...), the picker->admin-panel path this very method describes at :174-177 - times out: on_timeout() calls message.delete(), which for a plain Message is DELETE /channels/{id}/messages/{id}. The file itself states at :142-144 that Discord answers 404 for an ephemeral message on that route. The NotFound is caught and logged at DEBUG (:186-189), and the dead panel stays - the exact outcome on_timeout() exists to prevent, and invisible in the log.
findings.suggestion: Delete through the interaction token like CloseButton does (keep the Interaction that produced the message and call delete_original_response()/delete_followup_message()), or assert at send time that view.message is an InteractionMessage; and log the failure at WARNING when the message is ephemeral, since that is not the 'already dismissed by hand' case the comment assumes.
findings.unsure_why: Whether py-cord sets view.message to an InteractionMessage (whose delete() uses the webhook route and works within 15 min) or to a plain Message depends on the py-cord version and on how each caller attaches the view - both outside this section.

findings.trigger: A PrivateView subclass constructed with timeout=None (persistent, so that bot.add_view() can route presses after a restart - the docstring at :234-236 says this is done) whose auto-added close button ends up alone on a row (a Select occupies a whole row, or five buttons fill the first): the wrapper removes the X and sets self.timeout = 60. The view is now not persistent, and bot.add_view() raises ValueError('View is not persistent') at startup. Today's subclasses evidently avoid this (the bot starts), but adding a Select to a registered PrivateView tomorrow turns an intended persistent view into one that breaks startup - the 'never alone on a row' rule silently overrides the persistence the subclass asked for.
findings.suggestion: In the wrapper, if the subclass chose timeout=None, do not set AUTO_CLOSE_SECONDS; keep the X on its own row (or raise at class definition time with a clear message) so persistence is never changed behind the subclass's back.
findings.unsure_why: Whether any PrivateView subclass that is registered with bot.add_view() can reach the lone-X layout is outside this section; if none can, this is a latent trap rather than a live defect. Ranked medium because the failure, when it comes, is a startup failure.

notes: security_routes.py: all four routes carry @auth.login_required; /migration-help returning the token is B5 and not reported. Observations without a trigger I can state: (a) encrypt_token uses e.message on ConfigServiceError (:111) - if that class has no .message attribute the AttributeError raised inside the handler produces exactly the blank 500 the comment says was fixed; I cannot see services/exceptions.py. (b) In get_token_security_status/get_migration_help the failure branches spread **result.data; if the service ever returns data=None the TypeError is caught by the second tuple and the service's own error text is replaced by a generic 'Data error'. (c) get_migration_help's success answer is jsonify(result.data) without 'success': True while the other three routes add it - asymmetric for a front end that checks the flag; B5's addendum says the path works today, so presumably the JS does not check it. compat.py: gevent is opt-in and off in production; apply_gevent_fork_workaround replaces gevent's after_fork_in_child with a function that only logs, so whatever the original did after fork is skipped entirely - deliberate per its docstring. spawn_delayed: an exception in target goes to threading's excepthook / gevent's hub printer (stderr), not to the DDC log - same class of gap as E24 fixed for views; no caller visible. ddc_ui.py: CloseButton.callback on a public message defers invisibly and returns, so the presser sees nothing happen - intended as a safety net per the docstring. on_timeout's check of the private py-cord attribute _synced_message_views falls back to 'proceed and delete' when the attribute is missing (isinstance fails) - i.e. a py-cord rename silently re-opens the 'deleted whatever the message showed by then' problem the check guards against. PrivateView decides 'alone on its row' once at construction; items a caller adds afterwards (or a two-level PrivateView hierarchy where the parent's wrapped __init__ adds the X before the child's items) can leave the X mid-row or alone on a row without the auto-close rule being applied - no callers visible. A subclass with 25 components would raise in add_item(CloseButton()) and fail to open; unlikely. group_control.py: group_config_for() imports is_group_target from group_actions while the module top imports the same name from group_service - two implementations of the same predicate, could drift; I cannot see either. group_config_for() returns a config for an inactive group (active False) while group_entries() hides inactive groups - whether a button on an old panel of a deactivated group still acts depends on the caller checking 'active'. group_panel_embed() guards members is None, group_is_running() and _maintenance_button() do not (.containers) - if members_of() returns None for an unknown group, a panel redraw after the group was deleted raises AttributeError -> on_error -> visible 'An error occurred'; if it returns an object with exists=False the guards are merely inconsistent. admin_control_view passes channel_has_control_permission=True for the admin panel: per B2 and the SPEC's warning I do not report the missing channel check; the press-time check must live in the button callbacks, which are outside this section. The close button is appended to a plain ControlView here, not via PrivateView, so the 'never alone on a row' rule is not evaluated for the admin panel; with one of start/stop, restart, info, optional wrench and X that is at most five and fits. help_embed.py: content claims (/ss alias, 'Protected info (control channels only)') cannot be verified from here; both helps now share one builder as promised. Field sizes are far under Discord's 1024/6000 limits in English; not measured for other locales. config_cache.py: clear()'s docstring still says 'forces garbage collection' while the body says it does not; get_servers()/get_channel_permissions() hand out the internal list/dict (no copy), so a mutating caller edits the cache; get_config() copies shallowly, nested lists are shared. get_cached_config() bypasses the cache entirely despite its name. Whether set_config() is called again after a configuration save (otherwise the cache goes stale for 15 min and is then useless for the rest of the run) is outside this section. services/status/__init__.py and services/translation/__init__.py are pure re-exports and carry no plan names.
